intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for Gmail on Mac. Open an email in Safari or Chrome, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask. Lazur reads what is on screen and answers out loud. It can explain a thread, point at a button, walk you through a setting, draft a reply at your cursor, or take dictation with fn.
tldr: Open an email in Safari or Chrome and hold ⌥ ⌘. Ask “what do they want?” and Lazur answers out loud.
Say “reply, Tuesday at 2 works” and the draft lands at your cursor. You read it, then you send it.
Hold fn to dictate a new email. You get clean, formatted text at your cursor, in any app.
Lazur is not an add-in for Gmail. It works from your screen, only while you hold the shortcut.

blocks.text: What an AI assistant does inside Gmail on a Mac

An AI assistant for Gmail on a Mac works beside your browser, not inside Gmail. Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch at the top of your screen. Open an email in Safari or Chrome, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask. Lazur looks at what is on screen and answers out loud.
That covers five jobs. Lazur explains what is open. It points at a control. It walks you through a feature one click at a time. It drafts text at your cursor. Hold fn when you want to dictate.
It does not click for you. It cannot press Send, attach a file or move a message to another folder. You make every click. Lazur tells you where to go.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.
Is there a Gmail app for Mac?

Not from Google, as far as I can find. An Orbit for Mac blog post says there has never been an official Gmail app for the Mac. I found no Google statement that says otherwise. So you have three real options, and each one changes how you work.

rows: Gmail at mail.google.com with nothing to install
Turn on keyboard shortcuts first. Lazur works over this tab.
Gmail in its own window with a Dock icon
Install with More > Cast, save, and share > Install page as app.
Mimestream, Orbit or Apple Mail over IMAP
Check each app's pricing page and system requirements before you buy.
blocks.caption: Three ways to run Gmail on a Mac, with the setup note for each.

blocks.text: Lazur works the same way with all three. It reads the screen, not your mail account, so it does not care which window holds Gmail. The Chrome app is the closest thing to a standalone app. Some sites also show an install icon in the address bar, so look there first.
How to set up Gmail on a Mac before you add an assistant

Google does not publish a ranking of its Gmail Help articles. The Popular articles list is the closest proxy. It leads with account creation, sign-in, adding another email account, email security, bounced emails, categories and password reset. Those are the tasks Google chose to feature first.

items: Sign in or add an account. Ask Lazur where the account menu is, and it circles it.
Reset a password. Ask what the next screen wants. Keep the one-time code out of your voice, because audio goes to AI providers to get an answer.
Fix a bounced email. Ask what the error text means. Lazur explains it from the words on screen.
Sort mail into categories. Follow [how to turn on categories in Gmail](/how-to/turn-on-categories-tabs-in-gmail) for the tab setup.

blocks.text: How to ask Lazur what an email says

Open the message before you ask. Lazur reads the screen, so it can only explain what is visible. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask, “what is the actual ask here?” A good answer names the request, the deadline and the sender.

Take a vendor thread with a renewal and a long history. Open the newest message and ask, “what do they need from me, and by when?” Lazur should give you the one thing they want and the date. If the answer is vague, scroll up to the message with the price and ask again.
The common mistake is asking about a thread that is half on screen. Scroll to the part you care about, then ask. A summary of the top message does not cover the replies below it.
How to find a button in Gmail with Lazur

Gmail moves things around. Some options hide behind a small arrow or a menu. Ask Lazur where the control is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Scheduling is the usual case. The option sits behind the arrow next to Send.

items: “Where is the search box?” Lazur circles it at the top of the window.
“Where is Reply all?” Lazur circles the control in the open thread.
“Where do I schedule this?” Lazur points at the arrow beside Send, then the Schedule send option.

blocks.text: If the control is inside a menu, open the menu first. Lazur can only circle what is on screen. Ask again once the menu is open, and you get the right target.
How to walk through a Gmail feature step by step
Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. That matters when a setting has several screens and you want to stop partway.
Try “walk me through adding a Bcc.” Lazur points at the Bcc link near the To field. You click it. Lazur then points at the Bcc box and waits. Nothing moves until you click.

Written guides are better when you want the full list at once. Use [how to add CC and BCC in Gmail](/how-to/add-cc-and-bcc-in-gmail) or [how to create a signature in Gmail](/how-to/create-an-email-signature-in-gmail) for that. Use Lazur when you want only the next click.
How to write a Gmail reply by voice on a Mac
Most replies are three sentences you already know. Say them out loud. Lazur writes them at your cursor, and you read the draft before you send.

items: Open the email and click Reply. With shortcuts on, press r.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say what the reply should say, in plain words.
Read the draft at your cursor and fix any line that is wrong.
Click Send yourself. Lazur does not press it.

blocks.text: Here is a short example. Say, “reply, Tuesday at 2 works, and ask them to send the invoice before then.” Lazur writes a short reply that keeps those facts. The date, the yes and the ask all stay in.

blocks.title: Say the facts
blocks.text: “Tuesday at 2 works, please send the invoice first” gives a better draft than “reply nicely.” Give the date, the answer and the ask.
The usual mistake is leaving the cursor in the To field. Click into the message body first, then hold ⌥ ⌘. Text that lands in the wrong box is easy to miss.
How to turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts on a Mac
Gmail keyboard shortcuts are off by default. They only work after you turn them on. Set them up once, and the rest of this page gets faster.

items: Open Settings, the gear icon in Gmail, then choose See all settings.
Find the Keyboard shortcuts section.
Select Keyboard shortcuts on.
Click Save Changes at the bottom of the page.

blocks.caption: Main Gmail keyboard shortcuts for Mac, from Google's list.

blocks.text: Use the keys for quick moves and Lazur for questions. Press e to archive, then hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the next email wants. Keys handle the moves, and your voice handles the reading.
The full steps sit in [how to turn on keyboard shortcuts in Gmail](/how-to/turn-on-keyboard-shortcuts-in-gmail).
How to dictate an email on a Mac with fn
Hold fn and talk. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at your cursor, in any app. The Gmail compose box counts. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans, so long messages cost you nothing extra.

Three extras save time. Snippets hold lines you type often. A personal dictionary holds names and product words. Clipboard slots hold things you copied. Set them up once, then use them in every email.

blocks.title: Add names first
blocks.text: Dictate a client's name you have never used, and it may come out wrong. Add the name to your personal dictionary first, then dictate the email.
A morning in Gmail with Lazur, step by step
Take a morning with a long unread list and a meeting before lunch. Start with the newest message from your boss. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what it needs. Then press e to archive the mail that is already done.

For a message that needs a yes or no, press r and dictate the answer with fn. Ask for the deadline on anything that has one. Then say, “remind me to follow up Friday,” and Lazur adds it to Apple Reminders.
The morning goes wrong when you skip the read. A summary is a guide to the thread, not a replacement for it. Open the message if the answer will commit you to something.
How to search Gmail for old email on a Mac
Gmail search skips Spam and Trash by default. Many lost invoices sit in one of those folders. Search for the sender first, then widen the search.

items: from: finds mail by sender, such as from:dana.
has:attachment finds mail with files attached.
after: and before: narrow the dates, such as after:2026/10/01.
Press / to jump to the search box. Shift + / shows the full shortcut list.

blocks.text: Lazur helps when you cannot remember the operator. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask, “which search word finds attachments from one sender?” It explains the answer and points at the box. You type the search, so you decide what to keep.
The full list is in [how to search emails with attachments in Gmail](/how-to/search-emails-with-attachments-in-gmail).
Gmail storage and the 25 MB attachment limit
Each Google Account includes up to 15 GB. Gmail, Google Drive and Google Photos share that space. A large photo library leaves less room for mail.
For personal Gmail accounts, the attachment limit is 25 MB. Over that, Gmail removes the attachment and adds it as a Google Drive link. Work and school limits are set by the admin.
A MakeUseOf report from May 2026 says some new accounts may get 5 GB unless a phone number is verified. Google has not confirmed it. Check your own storage page before you plan around it.

Lazur can explain the message that says a file is too large. It cannot compress the file or add the Drive link for you. The steps are in [how to attach a file in Gmail](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-gmail).
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Gmail

items: Sending a draft without reading it. Lazur writes the text, but you own the send.
Asking about an email you have not opened. Lazur only sees what is on screen.
Expecting a click. Lazur points and guides, and it does not press buttons.
Saying a password or one-time code out loud. Audio goes to AI providers to get an answer.

blocks.text: Before you send, check three things yourself. Look at the To line, because a reply drafted from the wrong thread can reach the wrong person. Check every date and number, because Lazur can only read what it sees. Check the attachment against the 25 MB limit for personal accounts.
Pricing, trial and what Lazur does not do
Lazur has a free trial with no credit card needed. Paid plans are Pro and Power. Dictation is unlimited on both. Compare the monthly and annual options on the [pricing page](/pricing).

Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail or any other app. It works from the screen, not from your Gmail account. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report.
Where to start

items: Turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts in Settings > See all settings > Keyboard shortcuts.
Open one long email and ask Lazur to sum it up.
Write one reply by voice, then read it before you send.
Get Lazur from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Does Lazur need my Gmail password?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail. It works from what is on your screen, and only while you hold ⌥ ⌘ or fn. Keep passwords and one-time codes out of your voice requests.

faq.question: Does it work in Safari and Chrome?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works from the screen, so it works in a Gmail tab in Safari or Chrome, and in the Gmail Chrome app. The same commands also work in Apple Mail and Outlook.

faq.question: Will Lazur send emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, so it never presses Send. It writes the draft at your cursor, and you read it before you send.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not that I can find. An Orbit blog post says there has never been one, and I found no Google statement that says otherwise. The Chrome app and a browser tab are the two built-in routes.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my emails?
faq.answer: Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did on your Mac.

faq.question: Do Gmail keyboard shortcuts need to be on for Lazur?
faq.answer: No. Lazur uses ⌥ ⌘ and fn. Gmail's own shortcuts, such as r and e, are a separate setting. Turn them on in Gmail's settings if you want them.

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a free trial and no credit card is needed. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for the plans that follow.
